newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent into the red as prompt US mogas slides.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent into the red as prompt US mogas slides.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures went into the red on Thursday, shedding earlier gains in the wake of U.S. NYMEX gasoline losses.
December Brent at 1720 GMT was down 17 cents at $23.40 and off a high for the day of $23.92.
Dealers said the November NYMEX gasoline, which expires along with heating oil at the close of business on Thursday, had sparked the sell-off.
"Gasoline stopped the rot yesterday and it's gasoline which is taking down today," said a broker. "People are asking whether this market's in for another sizeable correction (lower)."
November IPE gas oil resisted Brent's fall to trade last at $219 a tonne, off the day's high of $221 but still up $1.75.
"Brent's moving more on technicals at the moment while people are still wary of the fundamentals on gas oil," said a broker.
The December gas oil/Brent spread finished at a stronger $5.30, up 20 cents on the day.
